extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: OVERVIEW

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: To uphold the highest standards of care for our members, we conduct claim and/or clinical reviews of

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: hospital admissions. These reviews assess the completeness, adequacy, and quality of hospital care

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: provided. Reviews are conducted in accordance with 42 CFR §476.71(a)(8)(ii) and other relevant CMS

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: guidelines.1, 2

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Scope

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: This policy applies to all Devoted Health plans.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Acronyms and definitions

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Initial Admission: An admission to the same or related hospital that is used to determine if a

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: subsequent admission meets the criteria for a readmission.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Quality Improvement Organization (QIO): An entity contracted by CMS to perform case review and

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: quality improvement functions.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Same or Related Hospital: Any hospital system or hospital that is part of a hospital system that

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: shares the same contractual hospital agreement and/or tax identification number with any other

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: hospital or system.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Same-day Readmission: Defined as readmission occurring between midnight and midnight of a

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: single day.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Policy statement

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: We may review readmission (re-hospitalization within a specified time interval) claims when a

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: member returns to the same or related hospital within thirty (30) days of the discharge date of a prior

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: admission. Consistent with CMS guidelines, we do not separately cover readmissions when they are

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: for a leave of absence, for the same or plausibly related condition as the prior stay, or considered

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: otherwise preventable.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: For the purposes of this policy, criteria for "same or plausibly related, or otherwise preventable"

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: include but are not limited to the following:

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● The same or plausibly related procedure and/or diagnosis as the prior discharge;

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● Procedures and/or diagnoses related to infections or other complications of care;

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● Acute decompensation of a coexisting chronic condition;

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● Medical decision making inconsistent with professionally recognized standards of care;

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● Insufficient discharge planning and/or post-discharge follow up, such as lack of coordination

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: between inpatient and outpatient services;

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● Premature discharge resulting in readmission, such as signs of post-operative infection or

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: abnormal test results at the time of discharge.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● Care that could have been provided during first admission (i.e., if the two confinements could

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: be related).

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● Readmission was medically unnecessary.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● Readmission was a result of circumvention of the Prospective Payment System.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: We will review claims and/or medical records for both admissions to determine if they are clinically

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: related and/or preventable. For additional guidance on readmission review criteria, please refer to

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: the Medicare QIO Case Review Manual and State Operations Manual.3, 4

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Exemptions from This Policy:

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Readmissions that are unrelated to the prior discharge are covered as two separate admissions.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: We recognize that there are times when readmissions are required as part of regular treatment or

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: due to extenuating circumstances and are exempt from this policy. Examples include, but are not

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: limited to, the following:

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● Behavioral/mental health and substance abuse admissions;

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● Planned chemotherapy treatments;

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● Planned infusion treatments;

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● Neonatal or obstetrical admissions;

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● Transfers from Out-of-Network to In-Network facilities;

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● Transplant and transplant-related admissions.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Leave of Absence/Planned Readmission:

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: If a patient is readmitted to a facility as part of a planned readmission or leave of absence, the

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: admissions are not considered two separate admissions. CMS requires the facility to submit one

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: claim and receive one combined MS-DRG payment for both admissions because both are for the

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: treatment of the same episode of illness. Examples based on CMS guidelines include:

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: "Hospitals may place a patient on a leave of absence when readmission is expected and the

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: patient does not require a hospital level of care during the interim period. Examples could

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: include, but are not limited to, situations where surgery could not be scheduled immediately, a

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: specific surgical team was not available, bilateral surgery was planned, or when further

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: treatment is indicated following diagnostic tests but cannot begin immediately."5

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Medical records for a leave of absence must clearly show that the readmission was planned and

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: related to the same episode of care. Leave of absence days are not covered by the plan and cannot be

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: charged to the member.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Same-day Readmission for Related Condition:

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: If a patient is readmitted to a facility on the same day as a prior discharge for the same or a plausibly

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: related condition, CMS requires the facility to combine the two admissions on one claim. Consistent

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: with CMS billing requirements, Devoted Health, may review same-day readmissions and request

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: medical records to determine if the readmission was related. If a patient was readmitted during the

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: same day for a same or plausibly related condition, Devoted Health will deny the subsequent

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: admission. The provider must adjust the original admissions claim to combine both stays on the

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: same claim to be eligible.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: If a patient leaves against medical advice (AMA) and then returns same-day to the same hospital, this

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: scenario will be considered a same-day readmission and should be billed as one claim.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Same-day Readmission for Unrelated Condition:

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: If a patient is readmitted to a facility on the same day as a prior discharge for symptoms unrelated to

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: the prior stay's medical condition, CMS requires the facility to follow different billing requirements. In

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: this situation, two claims are submitted, but the claim for the subsequent admission must contain

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: the condition code "B4". Consistent with CMS billing requirements, if a patient is readmitted on the

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: same day for an unrelated condition, two properly coded claims must be submitted to Devoted

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Health.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Transfer:

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: A discharge of a hospital inpatient is considered to be a transfer if the patient is admitted on the same

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: day to another hospital. A transfer between acute inpatient hospitals occurs when a patient is

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: admitted to a hospital and is subsequently transferred from the hospital where the patient was

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: admitted to another hospital for additional treatment once the patient's condition has stabilized or a

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: diagnosis established.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Effective for discharges on or after October 1, 2003, patients who leave AMA but are admitted to

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: another inpatient prospective payment system (IPPS) hospital on the same day as they left will be

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: treated as transfers, and the transfer payment policy will apply.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Claim submission and reimbursement

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: We process claims according to Medicare PPS payment rules unless otherwise specified by your

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: contract. Claims for readmissions that are billed separately but are not separately payable will be

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: denied and may be submitted as outlined below:

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● Readmission for the Same or Related Condition Within Thirty (30) Days

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ○ Submit a corrected claim (TOB 117) that references the original claim number;

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ○ Consolidate both admissions into one claim.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● Planned Readmission/Leave of Absence

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ○ Submit all admissions related to the episode of care on one claim;

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ○ Report leave of absence date span with Occurrence Span Code 74 (FL 35-36);

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ○ Report non-covered charges using revenue code 018X in FL 42.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● Same-Day Readmissions for Unrelated Conditions

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ○ Same-day readmissions for conditions unrelated to the prior discharge are reimbursed

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: as two separate MS-DRG payments. Billing should follow standard IPPS requirements

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: and include condition code B4 in FL 18-28.
